title: Turnkey procurement of 132 kV substation and transmission line in hilly terrain

items.title: Substation terrace levels deferred to design phase
items.text: The NAG-SS-02A package required the contractor to determine substation terrace levels and 33 kV gantry locations during detail engineering, indicating terrain adaptation was deferred to design phase under turnkey responsibility.

items.title: 132 kV transmission line procured via single-stage two-envelope bidding
items.text: The Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project (P162086) planned the 132 kV DIC 3 Ph. Nagar Untari - Gahwa transmission line package (IN-JUSNL-50790-CW-RFB-03B) using single-stage two-envelope bidding, but did not document a rationale for combining or separating substation and line packages.

items.title: Transmission equipment must suit tropical conditions
items.text: Equipment for transmission line components must be suitable for satisfactory continuous operation under tropical conditions, including moderately hot and humid climates conducive to rust and fungus growth, as specified in the SUPP_ARUNACHAL ARP_1 technical specification.

items.title: Technical compliance critical in turnkey rejections
items.text: In the Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project, bidders were rejected for failing to meet minimum technical scores, indicating that technical compliance in complex turnkey procurements may be a critical failure point even when pricing is competitive.

items.title: 132 kV double circuit transmission line from Jadugoda to Dhalbhumgarh
items.text: Design, Engineering, Supply, Installation, Testing & Commissioning of 132 KV Double Circuit Transmission line from Jadugoda (New) - Dhalbhumgarh (63.4 km).
items.relevance: Matches proposed turnkey procurement of a 132 kV double-circuit transmission line with full scope including design, engineering, supply, installation, testing and commissioning. Directly comparable in technical scope and procurement model.
differences: Project is in Jharkhand, not hilly terrain; terrain characteristics not specified in description.
Length is 63.4 km, unknown if comparable to proposed route length.

items.title: GIS substation upgrade at Tuensang to 132 kV
items.text: GIS Substation Package- NAG-SS-02A for upgradation of 66/132kV Tuensang Substation to 132kV level under Transmission System for Nagaland State associated with North Eastern Region Power System Improvement Project.
items.relevance: Matches proposed 132 kV substation upgrade via turnkey procurement. Includes GIS substation and voltage level upgrade, relevant to substation component of the need.
differences: Scope is substation upgrade only, not including transmission line.
Location is Tuensang, Nagaland — hilly terrain, but not the same region as proposed.
unknowns: Whether the substation includes 132 kV incoming transmission line connection
Exact terrain slope or elevation details

items.text: Turnkey Tower Packages TW01 & TW02 - Mizoram
items.relevance: Matches turnkey tower package for transmission line in hilly terrain (Mizoram). Relevant for transmission line component under turnkey model.
differences: Scope limited to tower packages only — no substation, no full line engineering or commissioning.
Does not specify voltage level beyond context of 132 kV system.
unknowns: Whether conductor, insulators, or OPGW are included
Exact terrain gradient or access conditions

items.title: Substation terrace levels deferred to design phase
items.text: The NAG-SS-02A package required the contractor to determine substation terrace levels and 33 kV gantry locations during detail engineering, indicating terrain adaptation was deferred to design phase under turnkey responsibility.
items.relevance: Demonstrates how hilly terrain constraints were managed in a comparable project by shifting site-specific decisions to the contractor’s engineering phase.

items.title: NAG-SS-02A GIS substation under NER Power Project
items.text: The NAG-SS-02A package under the North Eastern Region Power System Improvement Project (P127974) is a GIS substation package for Nagaland State.
items.relevance: Identifies a documented 132 kV substation package in hilly terrain (Nagaland) under a known project, relevant to evaluating packaging options for the proposed need.

items.title: 132 kV transmission line procured via single-stage two-envelope bidding
items.text: The Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project (P162086) planned the 132 kV DIC 3 Ph. Nagar Untari - Gahwa transmission line package (IN-JUSNL-50790-CW-RFB-03B) using single-stage two-envelope bidding, but did not document a rationale for combining or separating substation and line packages.
items.relevance: Shows use of competitive bidding for a 132 kV transmission line package in hilly terrain, but provides no evidence on packaging strategy (combined vs. separate) for substations and lines.

items.title: Substation package ASM-SS-01 procured separately
items.text: The appraisal for P127974 indicates that the substation package (ASM-SS-01) was procured separately, suggesting a deliberate decision to split responsibilities between civil/electrical works and major equipment supply.
items.relevance: Implies that responsibilities may be segmented by technical domain, which could inform packaging choices for the proposed substation and line.

items.title: Transmission equipment must suit tropical conditions
items.text: Equipment for transmission line components must be suitable for satisfactory continuous operation under tropical conditions, including moderately hot and humid climates conducive to rust and fungus growth, as specified in the SUPP_ARUNACHAL ARP_1 technical specification.
items.relevance: This defines the environmental service condition requirement for equipment under the SUPP_ARUNACHAL collection, relevant to hilly terrain in Arunachal Pradesh with similar climatic exposure.

items.title: 132 kV XLPE cable manufacturer must meet IEC 400kV PQ tests
items.text: The manufacturer of 132kV XLPE power cables must have designed, manufactured, type tested, and completed Pre-qualification (PQ) tests as per IEC standards for 400kV grade XLPE insulated cable as of the Notice of Award date.
items.relevance: This establishes a technical qualification threshold for cable suppliers under the NAG-SS-02A package, ensuring proven capability for high-voltage insulation performance in demanding conditions.

items.title: Tower bidders must demonstrate technical experience
items.text: Bidders for transmission line tower packages under the SUPP_ARUNACHAL collection must demonstrate technical experience through manufacturing facilities, plant and machinery, testing facilities, manpower, financial resources, quality systems, past performance, customer feedback, and banker’s feedback.
items.relevance: This defines the qualification criteria for bidders under the SUPP_ARUNACHAL qualification framework, relevant to turnkey procurement of transmission infrastructure in hilly terrain where proven capability is critical.

items.title: POWERGRID may waive minor bid deviations
items.text: POWERGRID reserves the right to waive minor deviations in bid submissions for transmission line tower packages under the SUPP_ARUNACHAL collection if they do not materially affect the bidder’s capability to perform the contract.
items.relevance: This sets an acceptance threshold for non-conforming bids under the SUPP_ARUNACHAL qualification framework, allowing flexibility without compromising contract performance capability.

items.title: Technical compliance critical in turnkey rejections
items.text: In the Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project, bidders were rejected for failing to meet minimum technical scores, indicating that technical compliance in complex turnkey procurements may be a critical failure point even when pricing is competitive.
items.relevance: This highlights a risk in turnkey procurement where technical evaluation rigor is essential; the user should ensure clear, measurable technical criteria are defined and weighted appropriately to avoid non-responsive bids.

items.title: Turnkey IT contract required 3–5 years operational support
items.text: In the Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project, a turnkey IT system contract required 3–5 years of post-implementation operational support for knowledge transfer.
items.relevance: For a turnkey substation and transmission line project, the user should verify whether similar post-commissioning operational support or training obligations are standard in comparable infrastructure contracts, and consider including them if critical to long-term performance.

items.title: Turnkey IT required integration of MBC, CIS, MDMS
items.text: In the Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project, a turnkey IT procurement required integration of multiple software platforms (MBC, CIS, MDMS), indicating that complex turnkey contracts involving system integration demand clear interface specifications and testing protocols.
items.relevance: The user’s proposed turnkey substation and transmission line may involve integration of protection, control, and SCADA systems; the user should determine whether similar integration requirements exist in comparable power infrastructure turnkey contracts and define interface and testing protocols accordingly.

items.title: Turnkey records lack delay or cash flow documentation
items.text: In the Jharkhand Power System Improvement Project, procurement records for turnkey IT and consultancy packages show evaluation outcomes but do not document schedule delays, cancellations, or cash flow mitigation strategies.
items.relevance: The user should confirm whether similar turnkey power infrastructure projects in hilly terrain have documented risk mitigation practices for delays or cash flow, and if not, proactively design such clauses into the procurement.

items.title: Define baseline environmental and topographic data
items.text: Define the baseline environmental and topographic data required for the substation and transmission line design in hilly terrain, including forest type, soil conditions, and wildlife corridors.
items.relevance: Secondary baseline data on physiography, climatic conditions, and forest types were collected for similar hilly projects (P127974) to inform environmental assessments and alignment planning.
items.label: Tentative

items.title: Confirm permit responsibilities between Employer and Contractor
items.text: Confirm which permits, approvals, and licenses the Employer will provide versus those the Contractor must obtain for site access, forest clearance, and import of equipment.
items.relevance: Contract conditions (NAG-SS-02A) explicitly assign responsibility to the Contractor for acquiring all permits and licenses required for performance, excluding those specified as Employer’s duty.
items.label: Tentative

items.title: Determine scope and authority for Site Acceptance Testing
items.text: Determine the scope and authority for Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) of control and monitoring systems, including who conducts it, what tests are included, and how defects discovered during SAT will be resolved.
items.relevance: In P127974, SAT was defined as an Owner-led activity with vendor support, including field tests not feasible in factory, and required correction of defects by the Vendor.
items.label: Tentative

items.title: Check if Contractor must provide access to qualification data via portal
items.text: Check whether the Contractor must provide access to their qualification data via a centralized portal (e.g., POWERGRID’s IoR portal) for verification during bid evaluation.
items.relevance: In SUPP_ARUNACHAL, bidders were required to grant viewing rights to their qualification data on POWERGRID’s IoR portal as part of bid compliance.
items.label: Tentative

items.title: Establish inventory control limits for critical components
items.text: Establish the inventory control limits for critical components (e.g., transformers, switchgear) during phased delivery to avoid overstocking or supply chain disruption.
items.relevance: In Jharkhand project (P162086), operational acceptance clauses imposed inventory caps on meter supply lots to manage logistics and storage constraints.
items.label: Tentative

items.title: GIS substation awarded to GE T&D India for INR 693.4M
items.text: The NAG-SS-02A GIS Substation Package under the North Eastern Region Power System Improvement Project was awarded to GE T&D India Limited, with an evaluated bid price of INR 693401152.00, notified on 2023/08/19, with a stated duration of 15 months.
items.relevance: This is a concrete award for a 132 kV GIS substation package in Nagaland, part of a hilly terrain project, with documented commercial fields including currency, price, date, and duration.

Ltd. & Transglobal Power Limited, with a signed contract price of INR 628739940.00, notified on 2024/10/08, with a stated duration of 24 months.

Terms of Reference



 



Consultancy Services for Power Procurement Costs Optimization



 



 



 



 



 



	
Background




The demand supply gap forecast is the difference between power demand and power availability. The different parameters that influence power demand and hence load forecasting are Weather Parameters, historical demand/load, load growth projections, historical life style &life style projections, festivals, holidays, elections, economic behavior of the country, policy decision of different statutory body/ Govt. etc. The different parameters that affect power availability from Generating units are maintenance schedule, Maintenance Planning of generating stations, Outage planning of generating units, life of generating units, long & short term power purchase contracts with generating units, fuel availability for generating units on short term & long term basis, various commercial conditions of power purchase contracts & their legal dispute status, various past, present & future decisions/ stays on various Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)& other related parameters.



As the cost of procured power is a very large part of the cost to serve for the organization, optimization in the cost of power procurement is very important. It is therefore important to continuously upgrade, strengthen & manage the Power portfolio in a distribution utility. The establishment of a formal Power management process is necessary to bridge the gap between the power demand and supply.



To reap the optimum benefits of the investments in Power Procurement, it is imperative that the investments are made most judiciously and efficiently.



Therefore, JBVNL requires the services of a reputed Consulting firm to work on power portfolio planning, who have the experience in load forecasting, achieving price optimization for Sale & Purchase of Power, management & optimization of Power Purchase cost by efficient scheduling of power plants & cost-effective disposal of surplus power.



	
 




 



The main purpose of this consultancy is to provide services to the client in preparing a sustainable & efficient power portfolio management solution comprising of Optimization of Power purchase cost, Short term & Real-time power management planning & DSM bill verification along with the Load forecasting services. The objective of this consultancy contract will be as under:



 



	
  Optimization of Power Purchase Cost

	
  Short term & Real-time power Management

	
  DSM bill verification

	
  Load forecasting.

	
  Hand holding support to utility staff




 



	
COPE OF WORK




Project scope would include solution software, implementation and three years Operational support. Software features would include mainly Medium term, Short Term and Day ahead Demand Forecasting, Day ahead and real-time power scheduling/management, integration with RLDC and SLDC, DSM bill verification, effective disposal of surplus power at competitive rate & suggest better power management techniques with the help of solution software.



Post implementation of the Power Management Solution, consultant shall engage for period of 3 Years Operational Support (which can be extended up to 5 years), wherein JBVNL shall have manpower of service provider engaged with JBVNL to transfer knowledge, handhold JBVNL staff, manage and build capacities for JBVNL



The service provider must guide & assist JBVNL in efficient power procurement & disposal related issues throughout the contract period.



 



	
Implementation: JBVNL intends to develop a power management tool that is designed to handle & optimize the power portfolio of JBVNL which would include effective power scheduling, effective disposal of surplus power, lowering down of PPC & Demand Forecasting functions.




 



Following are the components of solution



 



	
Medium term Planning: - It gather data from all stakeholders and forecast the data.




 



	
Day ahead power management: It gathers data from all stakeholders viz. Power Producers, Load Shedding, Weather forecast etc. to accurately predict power requirement during different slots of subsequent day. Schedule prepared from such forecast is automatically communicated to SLDC/RLDC.




 



	
Intraday power management: It gather real time data from all stakeholders viz. Power Producers, Load Dispatch Centers, Weather forecast etc. and proposes decisions to reduce real time power purchase cost through process of rescheduling, real time demand re-alignment and automated communications to power producers through SLDC/RLDC for backing up and backing down power capacities.




 



	
DSM Bill verification: System has capability of verification of DSM bill with existing utility data and configured DSM tariff. This may be a customized  




 



	
Handholding support: The service provider would ensure that tools run effectively with customized scenarios of JBVNL. Following are support services that are offered with the solution




	
Training to existing utility staff

	
Operational support for period of three years (which can extend up to 5 years).




Post product implementation:



	
The consultant will be required to provide advice for better load management, to reduce power procurement costs and suggest the strategies for shifting of load from peak hours to off peak hours to flatten the load curve.




 



	
The consultant shall provide analysis reports regarding load forecast and shall prepare the merit order of different sources of power from where JBVNL is getting power.




 



	
The system should review the existing intra-day, medium term & short term, day ahead and intraday power management process and redesign the process such that the DSM charge reduction shall reduce the Power Purchase Cost.




 



	
After implementation of the above said forecast, the consultant shall provide cost benefit analysis report on short, medium & intra-day basis including for peak/off-peak hours basis. This analysis shall be included as an output parameter of software tool.




 



	
The consultant should study & analyze the Indian Power Market & associate JBVNL in the purchase /sale of power through Power exchange & bilateral transaction.




 



	
The software should have the facility to store and analyze the data and use it for portfolio analysis and decision support.




 



	
Consultant must guide & assist JBVNL in efficient power procurement & disposal related issues throughout the contract period




 



	
The software should provide the following output parameters in addition to other parameters as will be required during the contract period.




 



	
Load forecasting (in MW) on short term, medium term and for peak hours & off-peak hours.

	
Power availability (in MW) on short term, medium term and for peak hours & off-peak hours.

	
Demand supply gap (in MW) on short term, medium term and for peak hours & off-peak hours.

	
Variation of load/power availability/demand supply gap with frequency, weather parameters e.g. Rainfall, Temperature (min, max & average), Relative Humidity (min., max. & average), wind speed, UI rate etc.




 



 



 



Features of Load Forecasting Module: Software will be deployed on basis of single geographical instance forecasting model to cover entire Jharkhand. JBVNL at any point of time would be able to get medium term, short term, day ahead and real time forecasting data for entire Jharkhand. For calculating demand supply gap (in MW) and for reducing Over Drawl (OD)/Under Drawl(UD) from the Indian National Grid, the Consultant shall undertake Load Forecasting on Short, (Daily, monthly & yearly) Medium term basis & long-term basis. In all the three scenarios the peak, off-peak and average forecast shall also be provided. The short-term forecasting data will be required to be prepared at 15 minutes intervals and updated on daily basis by using suitable weather data to be arranged by the consultant and other inputs required for accurate load forecasting. The consultant shall provide the necessary software tool for the above purpose and shall provide training to JBVNL employees for operating the software tool. The Consultant shall provide license for the software supplied in the name of JBVNL and the license should be perpetual.



 



While making forecast, the following factors shall also be taken into consideration along with other relevant factors:



 



	
For each month, both restricted and unrestricted forecast shall be made for peak as well as off-peak periods of the day. The seasonal variation in demand & energy requirement due to various factors such as paddy and non-paddy sowing seasons etc. should be taken in to account

	
Weather forecast

	
Overall economic growth projections, load curve, connected load, diversity factor and other techno-commercial factors; Likely impact of implementation of Demand Side Management (DSM) Regulations 

	
Projected efficiency gains due to implementation of T&D loss reduction initiatives and other improvement programs

	
The proposed methodology shall also be guided by the methodology adopted in the latest Electric Power Survey of Central Electricity Authority (CEA) for the State.

	
Any other tools which will help in power optimization.

(b) Site Acceptance Test (SAT)
The SAT will be conducted by the OWNER with support as required from the vendor after the system
has been installed and commissioned. The system will be subjected to a subset of the functional and
performance tests. The SAT will also include any type of testing that could not be performed in the
factory. Unstructured tests will be employed by the RLDC representative, as necessary, to verify
overall system operation under field conditions. Any defects or design errors discovered during the
SAT shall be corrected by the Vendor. The SAT includes the commissioning test, the functional and
performance test, and the cyber security audit after the installation of the delivered system.
(c) Commissioning Test
The commissioning tests shall be conducted by the vendor and include:

- Loading of the software and starting the system. At the option of the RLDC, all software shall be recompiled from the source or distribution media.
- Interface of the MDP software for all data sources and other systems that interface with the MDP software.
- Initialization and preliminary tuning of application software as needed.
(d) Site Cyber Security Audit
The site cyber security audit shall repeat the audit performed during SAT in every year during Annual
maintenance.
(e) Test Approval
The Vendor shall maintain a complete computer record of all test results with variance reporting and
processing procedures for approval by Employer. In the event that the MDP software does not
successfully pass any portion of the Acceptance Testing, the Vendor shall notify the Employer of the
specific deficiency. The Vendor shall promptly correct the specified deficiency, which will then be re-tested
until successful.
13. TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
Comprehensive training programs shall be provided to enable the efficient and effective use and
operation of the deployed system by users of the system, and to develop a self-sufficient software
support team within RLDCs.
Training shall include, where appropriate, a combination of formal training classes, workshops, as
well as continuous (informal) knowledge transfer from the Vendor’s technical specialists to the
personnel of RLDC during the deployment process and after the commissioning of the MDP software.
In-person/virtual training sessions could be offered at the RLDCs or any other locations of choice by
both parties.
(a) Training programs for system users
Training program for system users shall include but not restricted to the following:
- System overview including system functionalities and features.
- System configuration and operations oriented training.
